I got puffed walking in from the car park and going up the stairs, though sitting here I am alright, and since yesterday there is a sharp pain low down on the right side round towards my back that catches me when I take a deep breath or cough.

utterance: Your examination shows signs of a chest infection — pneumonia — in the right lower part of your lung: dullness and crackles there. I'd like a chest X-ray to confirm, and a blood test. reply: Pneumonia? Blimey, I thought it was just a bad cold. Do I really need to go off for an X-ray right now, or can it wait until after school finishes?

utterance: I'd like the X-ray today if you can — it takes just a few minutes and confirms the diagnosis and how much of the lung is affected, which guides your treatment. reply: All right, if it's that important, I will go straight over now.

result: Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms. Other lobes clear. No pleural effusion. Normal heart size.

utterance:
The X-ray confirms it: pneumonia affecting the right lower lobe of your lung. The good news is it's just the one lobe and your oxygen levels are okay, so you can be treated at home — no hospital needed.

Plan:
- Amoxicillin 500 mg, one capsule three times a day for 5 days — take them until finished, even if you feel better.
- Paracetamol 1 g (two tablets) every 6 hours as needed for the fever and chest pain.
- Rest, fluids, and stay home from teaching for a couple of days.
- No smoking exposure, and I'd recommend a flu vaccine and pneumonia consideration once you're recovered.

Safety net — come back urgently or call 000 if: your breathing gets much worse or you're breathless at rest, fever isn't settling after 48–72 hours on antibiotics, you cough up blood, you become confused, or you get severe chest pain. I'll ring you about your blood test result tomorrow, and I'd like to review you in 48 hours to check you're improving. Does that all make sense?
reply: Well, staying home from teaching isn't ideal with exams coming up, but I suppose I'd better follow the rules if I want to shift this.

utterance: Yes — resting now will get you back to your class quicker than pushing through. I'll review you in 48 hours, and call tomorrow with your blood results. Any questions before you head for the X-ray department and the pharmacy?
reply: No, that is all clear, I will go straight to get the antibiotics and then head home to bed.
